Approve. Test-only change; verified statically against the factory and the maasserver_discovery view definition (no suite run in this environment). (1) Correctness of the new setup: make_Controller(subnet=...) routes to make_Node_with_Interface_on_Subnet, which creates exactly one interface -- the boot interface -- on subnet.vlan (factory.py:1136-1156, interface_count default 1) and make_Node(interface=False) adds none, so rack.current_config.interface_set.first() deterministically returns the interface attached to the test subnet (current_config is created by the post_save create_default_nodeconfig signal, signals/nodes.py:199-203; Interface.Meta.ordering is ("created",)). (2) by_unknown_ip / by_unknown_ip_and_mac match the discovery IP string against StaticIPAddress.ip (models/discovery.py:57-81), so switching make_StaticIPAddress(ip=..., cidr="10.0.0.0/8") to subnet= is behaviorally equivalent (same default alloc_type AUTO, no interface attached); the rack's own DISCOVERED/AUTO addresses are empty strings, so the 1 -> 0 count transitions still hold. (3) test_associates_known_subnet / test_is_external_dhcp: the view joins the subnet on vlan.id = subnet.vlan_id AND neigh.ip << cidr and derives is_external_dhcp from the observer interface's VLAN, so placing the boot interface on subnet.vlan preserves the old vlan=iface.vlan coupling. (4) Consistency: make_RackController(subnet=...) is already used in api/tests/test_subnets.py:48-50, and current_config.interface_set.first() is the established idiom throughout api/tests/test_discoveries.py (test_read, the clear tests). The change removes the random make_Subnet/make_ip4_or_6_network call and the extra random fabric/VLAN previously added by make_Interface(node=rack), which addresses the overlap described in the commit message. The untouched tests still using the old pattern (by_unknown_mac, __known_mac, does_not_fail_if_cannot_find_subnet) do not depend on pre-defined CIDRs and remain deterministic. No bugs, security, or performance concerns.

src/maasserver/api/tests/test_discoverie.130: Deterministic, but implicit: .first() only returns the intended interface because make_Controller(subnet=...) creates exactly one interface (the boot interface, on subnet.vlan) and make_Node(interface=False) adds none. The factory also sets node.boot_interface explicitly, which would be the more direct and future-proof anchor (immune to a future make_Controller creating extra interfaces on the current config); .first() is fine here since it matches the idiom already used in this file (test_read, clear tests). Applies to line 143 as well. No change required.

src/maasserver/models/tests/test_discove.44: Same note as in the API tests: .first() is deterministic only because make_RackController(subnet=...) yields exactly one interface on subnet.vlan; rack.boot_interface would be the more explicit anchor if these setups ever gain extra interfaces. Applies to lines 55, 80, and 87 too. No change needed now.
src/maasserver/models/tests/test_discove.78: Semantics preserved: the maasserver_discovery view joins the subnet via vlan.id = subnet.vlan_id AND neigh.ip << cidr (and computes is_external_dhcp from the observer interface's VLAN), so creating the subnet first and attaching the rack to it keeps the discovery on subnet.vlan -- equivalent to the old make_Subnet(..., vlan=iface.vlan) construction. Worth knowing that make_Subnet(cidr=...) with no vlan puts the subnet on a new VLAN in the default fabric (make_VLAN -> Fabric.objects.get_default_fabric(), factory.py:1770-1773); that is harmless here because nothing else in these tests shares that VLAN.
